entry.title: March 2026 Southwest heat dome, Arizona +10 °C above normal

link.title: March 2026 Southwest heat dome, Arizona +10 °C above normal

entry.content:
A March 2026 heat dome pushed Arizona more than 10 °C above the 1991-2020 baseline.

ERA5 anomaly analysis places this among the most extreme warm events on record for the region at this point in the calendar. What makes early-season events like this consequential is not the peak value alone but the timing: it arrives before vegetation, soil moisture and water management systems are seasonally prepared for it.
entry.summary: ERA5 anomaly analysis of an extreme early-season warm event

entry.title: Fujairah drone strike seen from space

link.title: Fujairah drone strike seen from space

entry.content:
At 04:00 UTC on 14 March 2026, Meteosat imagery captured smoke rising over Port of Fujairah after a reported drone attack.

Ground access in situations like this is limited and contested. Satellites are not. Thick smoke plumes and thermal signatures were resolvable from roughly 36,000 km above the surface, giving an independent record of the event as it developed.

This is the part of remote sensing that rarely makes it into methods sections: observing fires, tracking impacts and documenting events when nothing else can get close.

Satellite: Meteosat. Time: 04:00 UTC, 14 March 2026. Location: Fujairah, UAE.
entry.summary: Meteosat imagery of smoke plumes over Port of Fujairah

entry.title: Unusual winter dryness across South Asia, January to February 2026

link.title: Unusual winter dryness across South Asia, January to February 2026

entry.content:
Between 1 January and 20 February 2026, more than 56% of South Asia received below-normal precipitation. Over a third of the region recorded its lowest wet-day count in the 1979-2026 ERA5 record.

The concern is sequencing. A dry winter depletes soil moisture going into the pre-monsoon window, which removes the evaporative buffer that normally damps early heat. Dry winters and severe pre-monsoon heat stress are not independent events in this region.
entry.summary: Below-normal precipitation across more than half the region

entry.title: Who can reach a clinic in time? Pakistan’s healthcare accessibility gap

link.title: Who can reach a clinic in time? Pakistan’s healthcare accessibility gap

entry.content:
This map shows the share of population able to reach a primary healthcare facility within 10 to 60 minutes. Darker blues mark stronger accessibility, lighter yellows mark gaps.

  • Balochistan has the lowest accessibility nationwide, driven by distance and sparse connectivity.
  • Southern Punjab and Upper Sindh show notable gaps within the first 30 minutes.
  • Mountainous terrain in KP and Gilgit-Baltistan extends travel times independent of facility density.
  • Central Punjab and the major cities benefit from denser facilities and better road networks.

These patterns point to where investment in mobility, facility siting and emergency response would change outcomes most.
entry.summary: Share of population within 10 to 60 minutes of a primary facility

entry.title: 2022 South Asia heatwave, atmospheric heat dome visualization

link.title: 2022 South Asia heatwave, atmospheric heat dome visualization

entry.content:
An animation of the 2022 pre-monsoon heatwave over Pakistan and India, built from ERA5 850 hPa temperature anomalies with 500 hPa geopotential height contours overlaid.

The geopotential contours do most of the explanatory work here. The anomaly field alone shows that it was hot; the ridge shows why the heat persisted rather than dispersing.
entry.summary: ERA5 850 hPa temperature anomalies with 500 hPa geopotential height
